At just 13 he became the youngest sole emperor of the united Roman Empire, succeeding his slain cousin Elagabalus as the last ruler of the Severan dynasty. Who was he?
Severus Alexander: Roman emperor from 222 to 235.
Founded in 1905 by Arthur Griffith, this Irish party's members established the revolutionary First Dáil and fought in the War of Independence — which party?
Sinn Féin: Political party in Ireland.
Born in Purbalingga and raised a devout teacher before the war, this man became the very first commander of Indonesia's armed forces during the national revolution — who was he?
Sudirman: First commander-in-chief of the Indonesian armed forces.
The first African ever to lead the World Health Organization, this former Ethiopian health and foreign affairs minister steered the agency through Ebola, COVID-19, and the mpox outbreak — who is he?
Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus: Ethiopian public health official (born 1965)
This retired Royal Navy vice admiral served as an equerry to Queen Elizabeth II before marrying her only daughter in 1992 — who is he?
Timothy Laurence: Retired Royal Navy officer (born 1955)
This nontrinitarian Christian movement rejects the traditional three-in-one God concept, instead viewing Jesus Christ as a supreme moral teacher subordinate to a singular Creator — what is it?
Held hostage by the Ottomans as a boy, this three-time Voivode of Wallachia is honored as a Christian hero in Romania for fighting the empire. Who is he?
Vlad the Impaler: 15th-century ruler of Wallachia.

Designed by Irish-born architect James Hoban in the Neoclassical style after a Dublin mansion, this building at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue has been home to every U.S. president since John Adams in 1800 — name this residence?
White House: Residence and workplace of the US president.

After leading an outnumbered army to victory at the Battle of Julu and toppling the Qin, this warlord carved China into Eighteen Kingdoms and founded the short-lived state of Western Chu — who was he?
Xiang Yu: Warload of Western Chu of China (c. 232–202 BC)
As the first Premier of the People's Republic of China, he helped orchestrate Richard Nixon's landmark 1972 visit while also serving as foreign minister during the 1950s — who is he?
Zhou Enlai: Premier of China from 1949 to 1976.
Which of these people was born first?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Which of these is a physicist?
John Logie Baird is a physicist. In 1928, the Baird Television Development Company achieved the first transatlantic television transmission.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Ingrid Daubechies is a mathematician. Baroness Ingrid Daubechies ( doh-bə-SHEE; French: [dobʃi]; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
What is the atomic number of Darmstadtium?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
What is the atomic number of Gold?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
In what year was Janet Yellen born?
Janet Yellen: Yellen is the Eugene E. and Catherine M.
In what year was Hippocrates born?
Hippocrates is also widely recognized for his contributions to medical ethics, being credited with the Hippocratic Oath that remains in use today.
In what year was Zakir Naik born?
Zakir Naik: Zakir Abdul Karim Naik (born 18 October 1965) is an Indian Islamic da'i and orator who focuses on comparative religion.
In what year did Guglielmo Marconi die?
Guglielmo Marconi: In 1929, he was ennobled as a marquess (Italian: marchese) by King Victor Emmanuel III, thus becoming the 1st Marchese di Marconi.
In what year did Ibn Khaldun die?
Ibn Khaldun (27 May 1332 – 17 March 1406, 732–808 AH) was an Arab scholar, historian, philosopher, and sociologist.
In what year was Phosphorus discovered?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.

Sukhoi Su-57: Komsomolsk-on-Amur Aircraft Production Association. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23 from?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet Union. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Who is credited with discovering Pictor?
Pictor: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pictor is a constellation in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere, located between the star Canopus and the Large Magellanic Cloud.
Who is credited with discovering Proxima Centauri?
Proxima Centauri: Robert T. A. Innes. Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Who is credited with discovering Stirling's approximation?
Stirling's approximation: Abraham de Moivre. In mathematics, Stirling's approximation (or Stirling's formula) is an asymptotic approximation for factorials.
Who is credited with discovering Yttrium?
Yttrium: Johan Gadolin. Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.

The first woman to officially attend a Dutch university, she became one of the Netherlands' earliest female physicians and, in 1882, opened the world's first birth control clinic — who was this suffrage leader?
Aletta Jacobs (Dutch; 9 February 1854 - 10 August 1929) was a Dutch physician and women's suffrage activist.
This unit of length equals one ten-billionth of a meter, or 100 picometres, and is named after a 19th-century Swedish physicist — what is it?
Angstrom (ONG-) is a unit of length equal to 1010 m; that is, one ten-billionth of a metre, a hundred-millionth of a centimetre, 0.1 nanometre, or 100 picometres.

This type of blood vessel typically carries oxygen-rich blood away from the heart, though the vessels serving the lungs and an unborn baby's placenta carry deoxygenated blood instead — what's it called?
Artery (from Greek (artr)) is a blood vessel in humans and most other animals that takes oxygenated blood away from the heart in the systemic circulation to one or more parts of the body.

This genus of deciduous trees includes 14 species across two subgenera, one found only in East Asia with low, multi-trunked growth, the other spanning Europe, Asia, and eastern North America. What tree genus is this?

Beech (genus Fagus) is a genus of deciduous trees in the family Fagaceae, native to subtropical (accessory forest element) and temperate (as dominant element of mesophytic forests) Eurasia and North America.

Native to eastern North America with resident populations as far north as Newfoundland, this crested songbird in the crow family has a black, U-shaped collar around its neck and a mostly white chest — name it?
Blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.
This condition results from inflamed, fluid-filled sacs that cushion friction points between bones, tendons, and muscles, commonly striking the shoulder, elbow, hip, or knee — what is it?
Bursitis is the inflammation of one or more bursae in the body.
This American Nobel laureate coined the term 'bioorthogonal chemistry' and studies cell-surface sugars called glycans from her professorship at Stanford — who is she?
Carolyn Bertozzi (born October 10, 1966) is an American chemist and Nobel laureate, known for her wide-ranging work spanning both chemistry and biology.
Present naturally in breast milk and added to infant formula, this essential nutrient is also a building block for a neurotransmitter that controls muscle movement — which compound?
Choline is a cation with the chemical formula +.
This legless, non-venomous lizard native to Europe is often mistaken for a snake despite having smooth, non-overlapping scales and semi-fossorial burrowing habits — what is it called?
Common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.

Caused by prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids like cortisol, this collection of symptoms includes abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and weak, fragile skin that heals poorly — what's it called?
Cushing's syndrome is a collection of signs and symptoms due to prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

This is the practice of communication between representatives of states or institutions aimed at influencing international events, serving as the main instrument through which foreign policy goals are pursued. What is this practice called?
Diplomacy is the communication by representatives of state, intergovernmental, or non-governmental institutions intended to influence events in the international system.
Once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil, these true seals of the genus Mirounga are named for the male's large trunk-like snout, with males weighing up to 4,000 kilograms — which animal?
Elephant seal are very large, oceangoing true seals in the genus Mirounga.
This ground-nesting songbird of Europe and the Palearctic sings its signature tune while hovering high over farmland and heath, and now also breeds in Australia and Hawaii — what is it?
Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.
Part of the dog family yet famous for a pointed snout and a brush-like tail, the 'true' members of this group belong to the genus Vulpes — what creature is it?
Fox are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to several genera of the family Canidae.
Caught from a tiny waterborne protist and common in travelers and children, it brings fatty, sticky diarrhea and abdominal pain a week or three after exposure — what is this parasitic illness?
Giardiasis is a parasitic disease caused by the protist enteropathogen Giardia duodenalis (also known as G. lamblia).
Named from Ancient Greek words for 'blood' and 'to make,' this biological process produces up to a hundred billion new blood cells per day in a healthy adult — what is it?
Haematopoiesis (from Ancient Greek (hama) 'blood' and (poien) 'to make'; also hematopoiesis in US English, sometimes h(a)emopoiesis) is the formation of blood cellular components.

Discovered in 2013 deep in South Africa's Rising Star Cave system, this archaic human left behind over 1,500 bones from at least 15 individuals, yet a tiny brain keeps its place in our family tree a puzzle — what species is it?

Homo naledi is an extinct species of archaic human discovered in 2013 in the Rising Star Cave system, Gauteng province, South Africa, part of the Cradle of Humankind, dating back to the Middle Pleistocene 335,000-236,000 years ago.
Aided by Soviet intelligence gathered on the American Manhattan Project, this physicist oversaw the first Soviet nuclear weapon test at Semipalatinsk in 1949 — who is he?
Igor Kurchatov was Soviet nuclear physicist (1903–1960).
With brownish-grey fur and a pinkish-red face, this cold-hardy primate is known colloquially by a wintry nickname referencing the snow in its habitat — which species?
Japanese macaque (Macaca fuscata), also known as the snow monkey, is a terrestrial Old World monkey species that is native to Japan.
This Hungarian-American biochemist spent years pushing past skepticism to lay the groundwork for mRNA vaccines, winning a 2023 Nobel alongside Drew Weissman. Who is she?

Katalin Karikó (born 17 January 1955) is a Hungarian and American biochemist who specializes in ribonucleic acid (RNA)-mediated mechanisms, particularly in vitro-transcribed messenger RNA (mRNA) for protein replacement therapy.
Representing the Nemean Lion slain by Heracles as one of his twelve labors, this zodiac constellation sits between Cancer and Virgo — which constellation?
Leo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac, between Cancer, the Crab, to the west and Virgo, the Maiden, to the east.
This Berkeley professor upended classical logic by proposing 'fuzzy' mathematics — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control, and more — who was he?

Lotfi A. Zadeh (4 February 1921 - 6 September 2017) was a mathematician, computer scientist, electrical engineer, artificial intelligence researcher, and professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley.
Sharing the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on nuclear shell structure, this German-American theorist became only the second woman ever to win that prize, after Marie Curie — who was she?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (ne Goppert; June 28, 1906 - February 20, 1972) was a German-American theoretical physicist who shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics with J. Hans D. Jensen.

This American theoretical physicist and science communicator, a professor at the City College of New York, won a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for a famous science-fiction author, honoring his work bridging science and sci-fi. Who is he?
Michio Kaku (born January 24, 1947) is an American theoretical physicist, science communicator, futurologist, and writer of popular science.
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this contractile tissue comes in skeletal, cardiac, and smooth forms and relies on the proteins actin and myosin to generate movement — name the tissue?
Muscle is a specialised soft tissue, one of the four basic types of animal tissues.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandin production, though it carries a risk of liver side effects. Name the drug?
Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.
Named from the Greek word for 'smell,' this hard, brittle, bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and is often alloyed for fountain pen nib tips — which element?
Osmium (from Ancient Greek (osm) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
This species of hickory tree, native to the Mississippi River region of the southern US and northern Mexico, is the official state nut of five states and the state tree of Texas. What nut is this?
Pecan (pih-KAN,; Carya illinoinensis) is a species of hickory native to the Southern United States and northern Mexico in the region of the Mississippi River.
Someone who specializes in matter, motion, and force through space and time earns the title 'physicist' — so what is the field they devote themselves to?
Physics is the scientific study of matter, its fundamental constituents, its motion and behavior through space and time, and the related entities of energy and force.
A strongly alkaline, water-soluble salt of carbonic acid, which compound with the formula K2CO3 is used in glassmaking and Dutch-process chocolate?
Potassium carbonate is the inorganic compound with the formula K2CO3. It is deliquescent, often appearing as a damp or wet solid.
This set of three positive whole numbers, like (3, 4, 5), satisfies a squared plus b squared equals c squared and forms the side lengths of a right triangle — what is it called?
Pythagorean triple consists of three positive integers a, b, and c, such that a2 + b2 = c2.

A brilliant English anatomist who coined the word 'Dinosauria,' meaning roughly 'terrible reptile,' he accepted that evolution happened but was an outspoken critic of Darwin's account of it. Who was he?
Richard Owen (20 July 1804 - 18 December 1892) was an English biologist, comparative anatomist and palaeontologist.

Created by Martin Odersky to address criticisms of Java, this statically typed tool blends object-oriented and functional styles, compiles to JVM bytecode, and can even transpile to JavaScript — which one?
Scala (programming language) is a strongly statically typed high-level general-purpose programming language that supports both object-oriented programming and functional programming.
Set in Miami, this NBC sitcom follows four older women sharing a home as they navigate friendship, aging, and daily life, led by Bea Arthur and Betty White. What show is it?
Silicone is a polymer composed of repeating units of siloxane (OSiR2OSiR2, where "R" stands for an organic group).
Members of the family Sciuridae, whose closest living relatives are surprisingly the mountain beaver and dormice, these rodents are native to the Americas, Eurasia and Africa — what are they called?
Squirrel (z)) are members of the family Sciuridae (sih-, -dee), a family that includes small or medium-sized rodents.

This medical term describes a resting heart rate above 100 beats per minute in adults, which can be either a normal exercise response or a sign of an electrical problem in the heart — what's the condition called?
Tachycardia is a heart rate that exceeds the normal resting rate.

One of five genera in the mackerel family whose members are collectively called tunas, this genus contains eight species, including the Atlantic bluefin, which can grow up to 15 feet long — name this genus?
Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Developed by Microsoft as open-source software, this programming language adds optional static typing to JavaScript and transpiles back into it — name the language?
TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
One of the oldest leaf vegetables eaten by humans, this fast-growing aquatic plant in the cabbage family shares its peppery bite with relatives like mustard, radish, and wasabi — what plant is it?
Watercress (Nasturtium officinale) is a species of aquatic flowering plant in the cabbage family, Brassicaceae.

This scientific discipline studies the structure, classification, behavior, and distribution of animals both living and extinct, and its name derives from the Greek word for 'animal' — name this field?
Zoology (zoh-, UK also zoo-) is the scientific study of animals.
Regarded as one of Formula One's greatest engineers, his car designs have won 14 Drivers' and 12 Constructors' Championships across three decades?
Adrian Newey: British engineer, aerodynamicist and motorsport executive (born 1958)

This American biologist founded a university institute for sex research in 1947 and gave his name to a scale measuring sexual orientation, after publishing landmark but controversial reports on human sexuality. Who was he?
First identified as a chemical in 1887 and later marketed as the drug Benzedrine, this CNS stimulant is prescribed today for ADHD and narcolepsy — which drug?
Designed in 1957 by a Soviet bureau and known to NATO as 'Coke,' this 50-seat twin-turboprop airliner is still license-built in China under a different name — which aircraft?
Antonov An-24: Soviet turboprop airplane. The aircraft was manufactured by the Kyiv, Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude Aviation Factories.
Most commonly caused by liver cirrhosis and its resulting high blood pressure in the portal system, this condition is the abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity — which one?
Ascites: Abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.

A North American bird of prey and sea eagle, found near large open water and old-growth forest. Its range spans most of Canada, Alaska, the contiguous U.S., and northern Mexico. This is the national bird of the United States. What is it?
Bald eagle: Bird of prey species of North America.
A red supergiant in Orion so vast that, placed at the Sun's position, it would engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars, this variable star is designated Alpha Orionis — which star?
Betelgeuse: Red supergiant star in the constellation Orion. It is usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky and, after Rigel, the second brightest in its constellation.
After scrapping its Sonic Cruiser idea, this American planemaker launched an efficiency-focused wide-body in 2004 with a first order from All Nippon Airways — which aircraft?

Thought to have originated in northern China, this widespread rodent is now dominant across Europe and much of North America, and gave rise to both a pampered pet variant and the standard laboratory strain — which species?
Brown rat: Species of common rat. One of the largest muroids, it is a brown or grey rodent with a body length of up to 28 cm (11 in) long, and a tail slightly shorter than that.
White, green, oolong, and black tea all come from the same evergreen shrub, simply processed to different levels of oxidation — name the plant species?
Camellia sinensis: Species of evergreen shrub. Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
Native to the rainforests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this flightless ratite is the fourth-tallest and third-heaviest living bird, trailing only the ostriches and the emu?
Sometimes dubbed the 'central science' for sitting between physics and biology, this field studies how matter is composed, behaves, and transforms in reactions — what is it?
Chemistry: Scientific study of matter's behavior and properties.
This inherited birth defect from a RUNX2 gene mutation leaves the collarbones underdeveloped or missing, letting the shoulders touch in front of the chest — which condition?
Cleidocranial dysostosis: Birth defect of the collarbones, skull, and teeth.
Blue above and orange below, this sparrow-sized bird dives for fish and nests in burrows dug into riverbanks — which species?
Common kingfisher: Species of bird. It is resident in much of its range, but migrates from areas where rivers freeze in winter.
Which tart fruit ripens on trailing evergreen vines with dark pink flowers, turning from light green to red as it matures?
Cranberry: Group of plant species bearing edible fruit.
Originally developed as an antidepressant, this fast-acting SSRI was later approved to treat premature ejaculation and was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2003 — what drug is it?
Dapoxetine: Medication used to treat premature ejaculation.
Marketed as Lanoxin, this centuries-old heart medication boosts contraction strength while slowing the heart rate, but can cause blurred vision and breast enlargement in excess — what is it?
Marked by itchy 1-2mm blisters on the palms and soles that clear in three to four weeks but often return, this form of dermatitis has no known cause — what is it?
Dyshidrosis: Inflammatory disease of the skin in humans.

Often tangled up with mood, temperament, and creativity, these neurophysiological states carry a degree of pleasure or displeasure — yet scientists still can't agree on a single definition. What are they?
Dubbed the 'father of geometry,' this ancient Greek mathematician's treatise Elements dominated the field for nearly two thousand years — who is he?
This neurodegenerative prion disease has trouble sleeping as its hallmark symptom, most often stemming from a mutation in the PRNP gene — what is it?
Fatal insomnia: Prion disease of the human brain.
Sold under the brand name Luvox, this SSRI antidepressant treats OCD and other anxiety disorders, with milder side effects than most in its class except gastrointestinal ones — what drug is it?
Fluvoxamine: SSRI antidepressant. Fluvoxamine, sold under the brand name Luvox among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
With a melting point of just under 30 degrees Celsius, this metal will turn to liquid in the palm of your hand — which element?
Gallium: Chemical element with atomic number 31 (Ga)
The tallest land animal alive and the largest ruminant on Earth, its closest living relative is the okapi — which long-necked African mammal is it?

This algebraic structure — a set paired with an operation that's associative, has an identity element, and gives every member an inverse — is exemplified by the integers under addition. What is it called?

Group (mathematics): Set with associative invertible operation. The concept of a group was elaborated for handling, in a unified way, many mathematical structures such as numbers, geometric shapes and polynomial roots.
About the size of a closed fist and enclosed in a protective sac called the pericardium, this four-chambered organ sits in the chest between the lungs and pumps blood through the body — which organ?
Heart: Organ found in humans and other animals.
Named for the English physician who first described it in 1832, this cancer is defined by multinucleated Reed–Sternberg cells in the lymph nodes — what is it?
Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of blood and immune-system cancer.
Named from Greek words meaning "over" and "formation," this condition enlarges tissue by increasing the number of cells rather than their size — which term, distinct from hypertrophy?
Hyperplasia: Enlargement of tissue due to cell proliferation.
Commonly known as chaga, this parasitic fungus grows on birch trees and forms a charcoal-like black mass often marketed, questionably, as a health supplement — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus: Species of fungus. Inonotus obliquus, commonly called chaga (a Latinization of the Russian word ча́га), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
The first woman to chair the Federal Reserve, this American economist later became the first woman to serve as U.S. Treasury secretary — who is she?
Janet Yellen: American economist and government official (born 1946)
Named the type genus of the walnut family, this group of deciduous trees produces the walnuts eaten worldwide, with China responsible for half the global supply — which genus?
Juglans: Genus of trees. Walnut trees are any species of tree in the plant genus Juglans, the type genus of the family Juglandaceae, the seeds of which are referred to as walnuts.
Caused by a thiamine deficiency often linked to heavy alcohol use, this brain disorder is marked by amnesia and confabulation, and frequently pairs with Wernicke encephalopathy — which condition?
Korsakoff syndrome: Mental illness caused by a lack of thiamine in the brain.
Together with pikas, this mammal family — comprising rabbits and hares — makes up the order Lagomorpha and includes over 70 species — which family?
Leporidae: Family of lagomorphs. Leporidae is the family of rabbits and hares (Lepus), containing over 70 species of extant mammals in all.
Developed under Kelly Johnson's Skunk Works team after the discovery of Germany's Me 262, this aircraft became the first jet fighter flown operationally by U.S. forces in World War II — which jet?
Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star: First jet aircraft in U.S. operational service.
Best known in its heptahydrate form as Epsom salt, this white crystalline compound (MgSO4) is also used in agriculture to fix soils deficient in an essential plant nutrient — what compound is it?
Magnesium sulfate: Chemical compound with formula MgSO4.
Awarded the 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering energy quanta, this German physicist originated quantum theory and lent his name to a fundamental physical constant — who is he?
Sold under the brand name Robaxin and developed in 1956, this centrally acting muscle relaxant treats short-term musculoskeletal pain but its exact mechanism remains unclear — what is it?
Methocarbamol: Medication for musculoskeletal pain. It may be used together with rest, physical therapy, and pain medication.
Nicknamed the 'powerhouse of the cell' after a phrase popularized in a 1957 magazine article, this double-membraned organelle generates ATP through respiration — which organelle?
Mitochondrion: Organelle in eukaryotic cells responsible for respiration.
Despite its name, this blister-agent chemical weapon isn't always gaseous, and to this day there is no antidote for exposure to it — what is it?
Mustard gas: Chemical warfare agent. There is no preventive agent against mustard gas, with protection depending entirely on skin and airways protection, and no antidote exists for mustard poisoning.
This medical specialty diagnoses and treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves, from epilepsy and stroke to Parkinson's disease — which field?
Neurology: Medical specialty dealing with disorders of the nervous system.
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This surgical medical subspecialty treats the ear, nose, and throat — organs connected via the Eustachian tube — earning its specialists the nickname 'ENT surgeons.' What field is it?
Otorhinolaryngology: Medical specialty of the head and neck.
From the Greek for 'the study of disease,' this medical field diagnoses illness largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — what is it?
Pathology: Study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.

Positioned behind the mouth and nasal cavity, this throat structure channels food toward the esophagus and air toward the larynx, with a flap of cartilage guarding against the two crossing paths — what is it?
Pharynx: Part of the throat that is behind the mouth and nasal cavity.

Derived in 1900 by a German physicist who proposed that an oscillator's energy could only change in discrete increments, this principle describes the spectral density of radiation from a black body at a given temperature — what is it called?
Planck's law: Spectral density of light emitted by a black body.
This common name describes small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs, especially popular in the UK and Commonwealth nations for larger swimming decapods — what is it?
Prawn: Common name applied to some types of crustaceans.
Ranging from Penguin Random House to countless small independent players, which broad industry covers making books, magazines, music, and software available to the public, in print or digital form?
Publishing: Production and distribution of media.

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?
Rock hyrax: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East.
Dropped out of Stanford to co-found Loopt, later led Y Combinator, then became CEO of the company behind ChatGPT — briefly ousted by its board in 2023 for not being 'consistently candid.' Who is he?
Sam Altman: American entrepreneur and investor (born 1985)
Encompassing several superfamilies and families, this taxonomic order groups together cephalopods that each have ten arms — which order is it?
These slow-moving South American mammals hang upside down in rainforest canopies, are kin to anteaters, and — despite the "two-toed" label — all have three toes on each rear limb; what are they?
Sloth: Group of tree dwelling mammals noted for slowness.
Native to China and Vietnam but now invasive across the US after spreading through South Korea and Japan, this planthopper prefers the also-invasive tree of heaven as its host — what insect is it?
Spotted lanternfly: Species of planthopper indigenous to Southeast Asia.
A colorless, non-toxic gas with an octahedral, six-fluorine structure, it's over 23,000 times worse for the climate than CO2 — which hypervalent compound is it?
Sulfur hexafluoride: Chemical compound and greenhouse gas.
Which calculus result approximates a differentiable function near a point using a polynomial — its first-order version being the familiar linear approximation?

Taylor's theorem: Approximation of a function by a polynomial. There are several versions of Taylor's theorem, some giving explicit estimates of the approximation error of the function by its Taylor polynomial.
Commonly nicknamed 'tree of life' from Latin, this genus of coniferous evergreens in the cypress family includes species native to both North America and eastern Asia. What's the genus?
Thuja: Genus of conifers. Thuja ( THEW-yə) is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).
Patented in 1956, this glucocorticoid treats skin conditions, allergies, and rheumatic disorders, and was the 108th most prescribed U.S. medication in 2023 — which drug?
Triamcinolone: Steroid medication. Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
Home to Polaris, the North Star, this far-northern constellation is also nicknamed the Little Dipper — which one?
Ursa Minor: Constellation in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Belonging to the same family as kangaroos but generally smaller, this Australian marsupial has also been introduced to New Zealand, Hawaii, and the UK — what is it?
Wallaby: Macropods of Australia and New Guinea.
With atomic number 54, this dense, colorless noble gas was the first to form a stable chemical compound, and now doubles as a general anesthetic and ion-thruster propellant — which element?
